heading: Disconnecting from an Existing BSP — Step-by-Step Visual Guide
content:
# Disconnecting from an Existing BSP — Step-by-Step Visual Guide

> Last updated: 2026-03-23 | Source: ManyChat Help Center (article 21611097151260), screenshots downloaded locally

heading: Overview
content:
## Overview

A phone number can only be active on **one** WhatsApp integration at a time. If your number is already connected to a BSP (360Dialog, Wati, ManyChat, Respond.io, Twilio, etc.) or to the WhatsApp Personal App or Facebook Inbox, you must fully disconnect before connecting it to Rio.

This guide covers the full migration path:
1. Delete the number from the current WABA (or remove BSP partner access)
2. Create a new WABA
3. Re-register the number under the new WABA

---

heading: Which Path Applies to You?
content:
## Which Path Applies to You?

| Your situation | Path |
|---|---|
| Number is on Cloud API via another BSP (no coexistence) | **Path A** — Delete number from WABA |
| Number is on Coexistence (WhatsApp Business App + Cloud API) | **Path B** — Remove partner from Meta + disconnect on mobile |

---

heading: Path A: Cloud API Only (Non-Coexistence)
content:
## Path A: Cloud API Only (Non-Coexistence)

### Step 1 — Delete the number from your current WABA

1. Log in to [Meta Business Suite](https://business.facebook.com/) with your business credentials.

2. Click **Settings** (bottom left corner).

   ![Meta Business Suite — click Settings](screenshots/bsp-disconnect/meta-suite-settings-click.png)

3. Under **Accounts**, click **WhatsApp accounts**.

   ![WhatsApp accounts section in Meta Business Suite](screenshots/bsp-disconnect/whatsapp-accounts-section.png)

4. Select the WABA associated with the number you want to remove.

5. Click **WhatsApp Manager**.

   ![Click WhatsApp Manager button](screenshots/bsp-disconnect/whatsapp-manager-click.png)

6. Locate your number and click the **trash can icon** to delete it.

   ![Delete number using trash can icon](screenshots/bsp-disconnect/delete-number-trash-icon.png)

> **Wait**: After deletion, it can take a few hours for changes to propagate. Do not attempt to re-register the number immediately.

---

heading: Path B: Coexistence (WhatsApp Business App + Cloud API)
content:
## Path B: Coexistence (WhatsApp Business App + Cloud API)

For numbers running in Coexistence mode, you need to do **two things**: remove the partner in Meta Business Suite, then disconnect from the WhatsApp Business App on mobile.

### Step 1 — Remove the BSP partner in Meta Business Suite

1. Log in to [Meta Business Suite](https://business.facebook.com/).

2. Click **Settings** → **Accounts** → **WhatsApp accounts**.

3. Select the **WhatsApp Business App** in question and open the **Partners** tab.

4. Click **Manage** next to the current BSP.

   ![Partners tab — click Manage next to BSP](screenshots/bsp-disconnect/coex-partners-tab-manage.png)

5. In the pop-up, click **Remove access**.

   ![Pop-up — click Remove access](screenshots/bsp-disconnect/coex-remove-access-popup.png)

### Step 2 — Disconnect on the WhatsApp Business App (mobile)

6. Open the **WhatsApp Business App** on your phone and go to:
   **Settings → Account → Business platform**

   ![WhatsApp Business App — Settings > Account > Business platform](screenshots/bsp-disconnect/mobile-settings-account-platform.png)

   ![Business platform list screen](screenshots/bsp-disconnect/mobile-business-platform-list.png)

7. Tap on the partner (BSP) in the list.

   ![Tap partner to disconnect](screenshots/bsp-disconnect/mobile-tap-disconnect.png)

8. Select **Disconnect**.

   ![Confirm disconnect](screenshots/bsp-disconnect/mobile-disconnect-confirm.png)

> **Wait**: Changes may take a few hours to fully refresh. Once complete, you can connect the number to a new platform.

---

heading: Step 2 — Create a New WABA
content:
## Step 2 — Create a New WABA

After removing the number, you need a new WABA to register it under. Two options:

### Option A: Via Embedded Sign-Up (through Rio/new BSP)

Go through the embedded sign-up flow. When prompted to select a WhatsApp Business Account, choose **Create a WhatsApp Business Account** (not an existing one).

> This is the cleanest path — the new WABA gets created during setup.

### Option B: Via Meta Business Portfolio directly

1. From [Meta Business Suite](https://business.facebook.com/), go to **WhatsApp accounts** and click **Add**.

   ![Meta Business Suite — WhatsApp accounts, click Add](screenshots/bsp-disconnect/meta-suite-add-waba.png)

2. Select **Create a new WhatsApp Business Account**.

   ![Select Create a new WhatsApp Business Account](screenshots/bsp-disconnect/create-new-waba-option.png)

3. Fill in your business name and required details, then follow the prompts.

   ![Fill in business details](screenshots/bsp-disconnect/fill-business-details.png)

---

heading: Step 3 — Re-Register the Number
content:
## Step 3 — Re-Register the Number

### Option A: During Embedded Sign-Up

Register the number as part of the embedded sign-up flow with the new BSP. The number is added automatically during that process.

### Option B: Manually via WhatsApp Manager (Cloud API only)

1. Open **WhatsApp Manager** for the new WABA.

   ![WhatsApp Manager](screenshots/bsp-disconnect/whatsapp-manager-add-number.png)

2. Click **Add phone number**.

   ![Click Add phone number](screenshots/bsp-disconnect/add-phone-number-click.png)

3. Fill in the WhatsApp business profile information and click **Next**.

   ![Fill in business profile](screenshots/bsp-disconnect/fill-business-profile.png)

4. Enter your phone number and click **Next** to complete OTP verification.

   ![Add phone number form](screenshots/bsp-disconnect/add-phone-number-form.png)

---

heading: Common Errors During This Process
content:
## Common Errors During This Process

| Error | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `#3441041` — "Phone number not associated with the business you selected" | Number still attached to old BSP's WABA | Complete Path A or B above, wait a few hours, then retry |
| OTP not received during re-registration | Number still locked from prior registration | Wait 24h after deletion before retrying OTP |
| "This number is already registered" during signup | WABA deletion didn't propagate yet | Wait 2-6 hours and retry |
| Partner still shows in Meta after removal | Propagation delay | Wait up to 24h; contact Meta support if persists after 48h |

---

heading: Key Rules to Remember
content:
## Key Rules to Remember

- **One number, one integration** — a number cannot be on multiple BSPs or on both a BSP and the personal WhatsApp app simultaneously.
- **Coexistence requires two disconnections** — Meta Business Suite AND the WhatsApp Business App on mobile. Missing either step leaves the number partially locked.
- **After deletion, wait** — do not immediately retry. Meta's systems need a few hours to release the number.
- **Create a new WABA, not reuse the old one** — the old WABA may still hold partner relationships or credit line attachments from the prior BSP. Starting fresh avoids hidden conflicts.
- **Credit line note (ManyChat-specific)**: ManyChat takes ownership of the WABA credit line upon connection. When migrating away from ManyChat, the credit line may remain. Creating a new WABA under your own Meta Business Portfolio avoids this entirely.

---

heading: WABA Setup FAQ
content:
# WABA Setup FAQ

> Last updated: 2026-03-20 | Curated answers to the most common questions Rio support receives during WABA onboarding.

---

heading: How long does WhatsApp business verification take?
content:
## How long does WhatsApp business verification take?

Business verification typically takes 2 to 7 business days after you submit your documents in Meta Business Suite's Security Center. In some cases it can take up to 10 business days, especially if Meta requests additional documents or if the information you submitted does not match what is in your Business Manager profile. You do not need to wait for business verification to begin onboarding with Rio -- you can create a WABA and register your number first, then verify later. However, without verification your account is limited to 250 business-initiated conversations per 24 hours and a maximum of 2 phone numbers.

See also: `05-business-verification.md`

---

heading: I didn't receive my OTP -- what do I do?
content:
## I didn't receive my OTP -- what do I do?

First, check that DND (Do Not Disturb) mode is not enabled on your phone, and look in your spam or blocked messages folder. Wait at least 2-3 minutes before retrying. If SMS still does not arrive, switch to the voice call verification option instead. Common causes include carrier-level blocking of international automated SMS, VOIP or virtual numbers that cannot receive SMS, and network congestion. If you are using a real SIM and SMS still fails, contact your carrier to ask if automated messages from international senders are being blocked. Do not attempt more than 3 retries in quick succession, as Meta will lock you out for 2 hours after 3 failed attempts.

See also: `errors/otp-failures.md`

---

heading: My display name was rejected -- why?
content:
## My display name was rejected -- why?

Meta's display name policy is strict. The most common rejection reasons are: the name is too generic (e.g., "Fashion" or "Technology"), the name does not appear on your business website, the name includes prohibited characters or symbols, or there is a language mismatch between the display name and your website. Your display name must clearly represent your specific business and must be verifiable on your live website -- Meta checks for this. A good practice is to include your display name in your website's copyright footer. If your name was rejected, update your website to clearly show the name, then resubmit. Capitalization and spacing matter: "BrandName" and "Brand Name" are treated as different names.

See also: `04-display-name.md`, `errors/display-name-rejections.md`

---

heading: What is the difference between a WABA and a WhatsApp Business Account?
content:
## What is the difference between a WABA and a WhatsApp Business Account?

They are the same thing. WABA is the abbreviation for WhatsApp Business Account. A WABA is a container inside your Meta Business Portfolio that holds your registered phone numbers, message templates, and billing settings. It is separate from the WhatsApp Business App you may have installed on your phone. Think of the WABA as the account-level asset that sits inside Meta Business Manager and connects to API platforms like Rio.

See also: `02-waba-creation.md`

---

heading: Can I use my existing WhatsApp Business App number with Rio?
content:
## Can I use my existing WhatsApp Business App number with Rio?

Yes, but there are two paths. If your region supports Coexistence mode, you can keep using the WhatsApp Business App on the same number while also connecting it to Rio's Cloud API. Your number must have at least 7 days of activity in the app before coexistence signup is eligible. If coexistence is not available in your region (or you prefer a clean switch), you will need to delete your WhatsApp account from the number first, then register it through Rio's Embedded Signup flow. Either way, your phone number itself does not change -- it is the same number, just registered for API access.

**Warning:** Coexistence is not available in all countries. It is blocked in the EU, UK, Australia, Nigeria, South Africa, Japan, Philippines, Turkey, and South Korea among others.

See also: `07-coexistence.md`, `customer-states.md` (State A)

---

heading: How do I migrate from another BSP to Rio?
content:
## How do I migrate from another BSP to Rio?

If your number is currently connected to another provider (ManyChat, Wati, 360dialog, Twilio, Respond.io, Infobip, etc.), you need to disconnect it from that provider first. Log in to the old BSP platform, remove or disconnect the phone number, and remove any credit lines the old BSP holds on your WABA in Meta Business Manager under Billing. Then wait 24-48 hours for Meta's backend to fully release the number. After that, you can register the number through Rio's onboarding flow. You will need to re-verify ownership via OTP and set a new 6-digit PIN.

**Warning:** Do not attempt to connect to Rio immediately after disconnecting -- the 24-48 hour wait is enforced by Meta.

See also: `08-partner-management.md`, `errors/partner-conflicts.md`

---

heading: What happens to my message templates when I migrate?
content:
## What happens to my message templates when I migrate?

Approved, high-quality templates transfer automatically when you migrate your WABA. Your display name, phone number quality rating, messaging tier, and Official Business Account status (if you have it) also transfer. However, rejected, paused, or pending templates do not transfer. Chat history does not transfer either. BSP-specific configurations (automations, flows, etc.) are tied to your old provider and will need to be rebuilt in Rio.

See also: `08-partner-management.md`, `customer-states.md` (State D)

---

heading: I'm getting error 130429 -- what does it mean?
content:
## I'm getting error 130429 -- what does it mean?

Error 130429 means "Throughput limit exceeded." You are sending messages faster than the API allows. The default throughput is 80 messages per second. To fix this, implement a message queue that spaces out your sends over time, and avoid burst-sending large batches all at once. Schedule non-urgent messages during off-peak hours. If you consistently need higher throughput, your account may qualify for an automatic upgrade to 1,000 messages per second if your quality rating is Medium or higher.

See also: `errors/error-codes.md`

---

heading: My account has been disabled -- what do I do?
content:
## My account has been disabled -- what do I do?

If Meta has disabled your WABA, it is typically due to a Commerce Policy violation, quality issues, or suspicious activity. Your first step is to check Meta Business Support Home (accessible from Meta Business Manager) to see the specific reason. You can appeal the decision through Meta's Account Quality tool in Business Manager. If the appeal is unsuccessful, your only option is to create a new WABA with a new phone number. Rio cannot connect to a disabled or banned WABA -- the account must be restored by Meta before any BSP can use it.

**Warning:** If your business falls into a prohibited category (gambling, alcohol, adult content, drugs, etc.), the WhatsApp Business API is not available for your use case and the ban will not be overturned.

See also: `errors/account-restrictions.md`

---

heading: How many messages can I send per day?
content:
## How many messages can I send per day?

It depends on your messaging tier. Before business verification, you are limited to 250 business-initiated conversations per 24 hours. After verification, you start at Tier 1 (1,000 conversations per 24 hours) and can escalate: Tier 2 is 10,000, Tier 3 is 100,000, and Tier 4 is unlimited. Tier upgrades happen automatically when you use at least 50% of your current tier's capacity over 7 days while maintaining a High or Medium quality rating. You can always respond to incoming customer messages regardless of your tier limit.

See also: `errors/messaging-limits.md`

---

heading: What documents do I need for business verification?
content:
## What documents do I need for business verification?

You need at least one official document that shows your legal business name and your business address or phone number. Accepted documents include: business license, certificate of incorporation, tax or VAT registration certificate, government-issued business registration, utility bills, or bank statements. The name and address on the document must match exactly what is entered in your Meta Business Manager profile. Non-English documents require a certified English translation with an official stamp. Documents must be high-resolution, uncropped, and not expired (some must be less than 1 year old).

See also: `05-business-verification.md`, `errors/business-verification-failures.md`

---

heading: How long do I have to wait after a failed business verification?
content:
## How long do I have to wait after a failed business verification?

There is no fixed mandatory waiting period after a failed verification, but you should not resubmit immediately with the same documents that were rejected. First, fix the issue that caused the rejection -- typically a name mismatch between your document and your Business Manager profile, an expired document, or a document that does not clearly show your business name and address. Once corrected, you can resubmit. If Meta keeps rejecting your submissions, try a different document type. The review process takes another 2-7 business days each time you resubmit.

See also: `05-business-verification.md`, `errors/business-verification-failures.md`

---

heading: I forgot my 6-digit PIN -- what do I do?
content:
## I forgot my 6-digit PIN -- what do I do?

The 6-digit two-step verification PIN is a security code you set when your number was first registered for WhatsApp (possibly in the WhatsApp Business App, before you ever connected to Rio). If you set a recovery email when creating the PIN, you can request a reset link via that email. If you did not set a recovery email, you must wait 7 days before the PIN can be reset. During this 7-day period, your number cannot be registered or migrated. This is one of the most common blockers during onboarding -- always record your PIN in a safe place.

See also: `06-two-step-verification.md`

---

heading: Why does my display name show a phone number instead of my business name?
content:
## Why does my display name show a phone number instead of my business name?

This means your display name is still pending approval from Meta. Until Meta approves your display name, your phone number is shown to customers instead. Display name reviews typically take 1-3 business days but can take longer. While pending, your account is limited to 250 business-initiated conversations per 24 hours. This does not block your connection to Rio -- you can still send and receive messages while waiting for approval. If your display name has been pending for more than 5 business days, check Meta Business Support Home for any issues.

See also: `04-display-name.md`

---

heading: What's the difference between the WhatsApp Business App and the Cloud API?
content:
## What's the difference between the WhatsApp Business App and the Cloud API?

The WhatsApp Business App is a free mobile application designed for small businesses to chat with customers one-on-one. The Cloud API (which Rio uses) is a programmatic interface hosted by Meta that allows businesses to send and receive messages at scale, use automations, integrate with CRMs, and handle high volumes of conversations. The app is manual and limited to one device at a time; the API supports multiple agents, chatbots, and system integrations. Using the API requires a WABA, a registered phone number, and a connection through a BSP like Rio.

See also: `01-prerequisites.md`, `07-coexistence.md`

---

heading: Can I keep using the WhatsApp Business App after connecting to Rio?
content:
## Can I keep using the WhatsApp Business App after connecting to Rio?

Only if your region supports Coexistence mode. If you set up via the coexistence path, both the app and the API remain active on the same number. Messages sent from either side appear on both as "echo messages." However, messages sent from the app are free but do not trigger Rio automations or workflows. If coexistence is not available in your country, connecting to the Cloud API disconnects the WhatsApp Business App and you will no longer be able to use it on that number.

See also: `07-coexistence.md`

---

heading: My OTP verification is blocked for 7 days -- why?
content:
## My OTP verification is blocked for 7 days -- why?

A 7-day OTP block is usually caused by a two-step verification PIN conflict, not by OTP rate limiting. If your number previously had a PIN set (often from the WhatsApp Business App) and someone attempted to register or migrate the number without entering the correct PIN, Meta enforces a 7-day security cooldown. A separate scenario: after 10 failed OTP entries during a migration flow, Meta enforces a 72-hour lockout (not 7 days). In either case, you must wait the full period -- there is no way to speed it up. Do not attempt any further verification during the cooldown.

See also: `errors/otp-failures.md`, `06-two-step-verification.md`

---

heading: Error 131049 -- my marketing message wasn't delivered?
content:
## Error 131049 -- my marketing message wasn't delivered?

Error 131049 means Meta intentionally chose not to deliver your marketing message. This happens when the recipient has already received 6 or more marketing messages from other businesses within a certain timeframe. Meta caps marketing messages per user to prevent inbox saturation. This is not a problem with your account -- it is a per-recipient limit. To work around it: switch your template to a Utility or Authentication category if the content qualifies, or wait 2-7 days before retrying. Segmenting your audience and spreading sends over time also helps reduce the frequency of this error.

See also: `errors/error-codes.md`

---

heading: How do I know if my WABA is business-owned or BSP-owned?
content:
## How do I know if my WABA is business-owned or BSP-owned?

In Meta Business Manager, go to Business Settings, then WhatsApp Accounts. If the WABA appears directly under your own Business Portfolio, it is business-owned and you have full control. If it was created by a BSP (like Wati or Gupshup) under their portfolio and shared with you, it is BSP-owned. BSP-owned WABAs are harder to migrate because you may need the BSP's cooperation to release or transfer the account. Always ask your current provider whether the WABA is in your name or theirs before starting a migration. Rio's onboarding creates business-owned WABAs by default.

See also: `08-partner-management.md`, `competitor-docs/waba-ownership.md`

---

heading: What is an Official Business Account (OBA) and do I need one?
content:
## What is an Official Business Account (OBA) and do I need one?

An Official Business Account (also called "blue tick" or "green tick") is a special Meta-verified status that shows a verification badge next to your display name in WhatsApp. It signals to customers that your business is authentic. You do not need an OBA to use Rio or the WhatsApp Business API -- it is optional and purely cosmetic from a functionality standpoint. OBA status requires completed business verification, an approved display name, and significant brand recognition (typically evidenced by media coverage, a strong web presence, or high search volume). Most small and medium businesses will not qualify, and that is perfectly fine -- the API works identically with or without the badge.

See also: `04-display-name.md`, `05-business-verification.md`

---

heading: The embedded signup flow failed or I got a "user canceled" error -- what do I do?
content:
## The embedded signup flow failed or I got a "user canceled" error -- what do I do?

This is a common issue, and one of the most frequently searched topics in our knowledge base. "User canceled" errors during Meta's Embedded Signup usually mean the popup was blocked by your browser, you accidentally closed the Meta login window, or there was a session timeout. First, make sure popup blockers are disabled for the signup page. Use Chrome or Edge (Safari can be inconsistent). Try the flow again in a private/incognito window. If you see "authorization failed," make sure you are logging in with a Meta account that has admin access to your Business Portfolio -- employee-level access will not work. If the error persists after multiple attempts, clear your browser cache and try again.

See also: `errors/embedded-signup-errors.md`, `01-prerequisites.md`

---

heading: My phone number is not working or cannot be registered -- why?
content:
## My phone number is not working or cannot be registered -- why?

Only real SIM-based mobile numbers and business landlines capable of receiving voice calls are reliably supported for WABA registration. Virtual numbers from Google Voice, Skype, TextNow, Burner, Hushed, and similar apps will not work. VOIP numbers from providers like Twilio or Vonage may work initially but are unreliable long-term. If your number is already registered with another BSP, it must be released first (see the migration FAQ above). Also confirm your number is in the correct E.164 format (country code + number, no spaces or dashes) and that it can actually receive SMS or voice calls right now.

See also: `errors/phone-number-issues.md`, `03-phone-number-setup.md`, `customer-states.md`

heading: Prerequisites for Connecting Your WhatsApp Business API to Rio
content:
# Prerequisites for Connecting Your WhatsApp Business API to Rio

> Last updated: 2026-03-20 | Sources: Notion (Rio), 360dialog, Wati, ManyChat, Respond.io, Infobip, Meta Official

heading: Overview
content:
## Overview

Before you can connect your WhatsApp Business API to Rio, you need a set of Meta assets in place: a Meta account with Business Portfolio access, a WhatsApp Business Account (WABA), a registered phone number, and a compliant display name. Business verification is not always required to begin, but it unlocks higher messaging limits and is often triggered by Meta during onboarding. This file covers everything you need to have ready before starting the Rio setup flow.

**Note on Meta App Review:** You do not need to worry about Meta App Review or requesting app-level permissions yourself. Rio handles app-level permissions as part of the Embedded Signup flow. You will not be asked to submit a Meta App Review request.

---

heading: Meta Account Requirements
content:
## Meta Account Requirements

The person doing setup must have a **Facebook/Meta account** that can access Meta Business Suite at https://business.facebook.com/. This is typically a personal Facebook login used as an admin identity — it does not need to be a "business" Facebook account, but it must have admin-level access to the Business Portfolio used for WhatsApp.

**Key points:**
- The Meta login must be able to access Meta Business Suite
- The person setting up must have **Admin-level access** to the Business Portfolio (not employee-only access), because creating and selecting WhatsApp assets during Embedded Signup requires admin rights
- If a client is setting up through an agency, they must use the **client's own Business account**, not the agency's (per ManyChat and Meta documentation — agency-owned portfolios cause rejection and blocking in Embedded Signup flows)

---

heading: Business Portfolio Setup
content:
## Business Portfolio Setup

Meta requires a **Meta Business Portfolio** (also called Business Manager) to use the WhatsApp Business APIs. This is the container that holds the WABA and all related assets.

**Requirements:**
- Must be a Business Portfolio **owned by the business itself**, not managed on behalf of the business by an agency
- Must have complete business information filled in (legal name, address, website, phone)
- The person onboarding must have admin access to this portfolio

**How to create one:** https://business.facebook.com/

According to 360dialog docs, incomplete Business Info (missing legal name, address, website, or phone) causes the WABA to become restricted with an unclear status.

---

heading: Required Business Information
content:
## Required Business Information

The following business information must be ready and accurate before starting. It must be consistent across Meta Business Manager, the WABA, the business website, and any supporting documents.

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| Legal business name | Must match exactly across Meta, website, and documents |
| Business address | Street address, city, state/province, country |
| Business website | Must be live, publicly accessible, SSL/HTTPS |
| Business phone number | Contact number (can differ from WhatsApp number) |
| Business email | According to ManyChat docs: domain should match website (contact@yourbusiness.com, not gmail.com) |
| Business category | Selected during WABA creation |
| Billing currency | Your WABA must be set up with **USD** as the billing currency. A currency mismatch can cause messaging failures even after a successful connection. |

**Website requirements (per multiple competitors):**
- Live and publicly accessible
- Contains business name or logo
- Contains contact information (address, phone, email)
- Secured with SSL/HTTPS (360dialog explicitly requires this)
- According to ManyChat docs: should include address, phone, social media links, product/service description, and a copyright footer with the business name

According to ManyChat: a missing or incomplete website is a leading cause of account disabled errors during signup ("This account was disabled because the website indicated in your Business Manager profile does not contain the necessary information to determine that your business complies with our Commerce Policy").

---

heading: Admin Access Requirements
content:
## Admin Access Requirements

The person completing setup needs:
- Admin role on the Meta Business Portfolio
- Ability to create or select WhatsApp Business Accounts within that portfolio
- Access to the phone number that will be registered (to receive SMS or voice OTP during setup)

If using an agency setup flow, the agency must access the client's Business Portfolio directly — not proxy through their own portfolio.

---

heading: What to Have Ready Before Starting
content:
## What to Have Ready Before Starting

**Checklist (drawn from Rio Notion, Meta official, and multiple BSP docs):**

- [ ] Meta login with access to Meta Business Suite
- [ ] A Business Portfolio owned by the business (not an agency portfolio)
- [ ] Admin access to that Business Portfolio for the person doing setup
- [ ] Legal business name ready (exactly as registered)
- [ ] Business address ready
- [ ] Live business website with SSL
- [ ] Business email (ideally matching website domain)
- [ ] Phone number that can receive SMS or voice call for OTP — see 03-phone-number-setup.md for number type rules
- [ ] Display name ready and policy-compliant — see 04-display-name.md for rules; the display name must already be **visible on your business website** (e.g., in the footer or About page) before starting setup, as Meta checks this during review
- [ ] WABA billing currency set to **USD**
- [ ] Acceptance of WhatsApp Business Platform policies:
  - https://business.whatsapp.com/policy
  - https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/meta-terms-whatsapp-business
  - https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/business-solution-terms

**What is NOT required to start (but needed to scale):**
- Meta Verified (paid) — not required
- Meta Business Verification — not required at the moment of onboarding, but required for higher messaging limits (above 250 business-initiated conversations per rolling 24-hour period) and more than 2 registered phone numbers

---

heading: Business Verification (When It Matters)
content:
## Business Verification (When It Matters)

Business verification is the process of submitting legal documents in Meta Business Suite's Security Center (https://www.facebook.com/business/help/2058515294227817).

**Unverified limits:**
- Up to 2 phone numbers registered
- 250 business-initiated conversations per rolling 24-hour period (per Respond.io and ManyChat)

**Verified limits:**
- Up to 20 phone numbers
- 2,000+ business-initiated conversations, with automatic tier escalation available

**When verification is triggered:**
- Some Embedded Signup flows trigger a verification requirement before a WABA can be created, depending on account state (per Meta official docs on embedded signup errors)
- Meta may require verification if the business is in a restricted category or if signals flag the account

**Documents accepted (per Meta official and Infobip docs):**
- Business license
- Certificate of incorporation or formation
- Tax or VAT registration certificate
- Government-issued business registration
- Utility bills or bank statements (for address verification)

**Document rules:**
- Must clearly show legal business name and address
- Must match the information in Business Manager exactly
- Non-English documents require an officially stamped certified English translation
- Must not be expired (Infobip: certain documents must be less than 1 year old)
- Must be high-resolution and uncropped

---

heading: Pricing and Billing
content:
## Pricing and Billing

Rio uses Meta's **per-message pricing (PMP)** model. The older conversation-based pricing (CBP) model was deprecated as of July 1, 2025.

Under PMP, Meta charges per message sent. The rate varies by message type (marketing, utility, authentication, service) and by the destination country. **Do not rely on any pricing tables that show per-conversation rates** — those figures are outdated. Rio will provide current rate information when you sign up.

---

heading: Legal and Compliance Prerequisites
content:
## Legal and Compliance Prerequisites

By connecting to Rio, you accept that Rio (as your WhatsApp Business Solution Provider) will process WhatsApp Business Solution data on your behalf. You must:

- Comply with WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy (consent/opt-in, prohibited content, user experience, data protection): https://business.whatsapp.com/policy
- Agree to WhatsApp Business Solution Terms: https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/business-solution-terms
- Understand that templates are required for any business-initiated (outbound) messaging — session messages are free within 24 hours of a customer reply, but proactive outreach requires approved templates

heading: Common Issues at the Prerequisites Stage
content:
## Common Issues at the Prerequisites Stage

### Common Issues

- **Issue**: Agency-owned Business Portfolio blocks setup
  - **Symptom**: Embedded Signup flow fails or WABA assets cannot be created
  - **Cause**: The Business Portfolio is owned by an agency, not the business itself
  - **Fix**: Customer must create their own Business Portfolio at business.facebook.com, or the agency must operate within the client's portfolio

- **Issue**: Missing or incomplete business website causes account disabled error
  - **Symptom**: Error during signup: "This account was disabled because the website indicated in your Business Manager profile does not contain the necessary information..."
  - **Cause**: Business website missing required information or doesn't match Business Manager profile
  - **Fix**: Add address, phone, email, social media links, product/service description, and copyright footer to website; update Business Manager profile to match

- **Issue**: Email domain mismatch triggers Trust & Safety review
  - **Symptom**: Business verification rejected or compliance warning appears
  - **Cause**: Business email uses generic domain (gmail.com) instead of matching website domain
  - **Fix**: Create a business email on the same domain as the website (contact@mybusiness.com) and update Meta Business Manager

- **Issue**: Business verification required before WABA creation
  - **Symptom**: Embedded Signup flow halts with a verification requirement error
  - **Cause**: Meta's background Commerce Policy check flagged the account, or the business is in a category that requires verification upfront
  - **Fix**: Complete business verification in Security Center (https://www.facebook.com/business/help/2058515294227817) before proceeding

heading: Creating Your WhatsApp Business Account (WABA) with Rio
content:
# Creating Your WhatsApp Business Account (WABA) with Rio

> Last updated: 2026-03-20 | Sources: Notion (Rio), 360dialog, Wati, ManyChat, Respond.io, Infobip, Meta Official

heading: Overview
content:
## Overview

A WhatsApp Business Account (WABA) is the container inside Meta Business Manager that holds your WhatsApp assets — phone numbers, templates, and messaging settings. It is distinct from the WhatsApp Business App. When setting up with Rio, you will create a new WABA or connect an existing one through Rio's Embedded Signup flow. This file covers the setup mechanics, WABA concepts, and common creation errors.

**All Rio customers use the Embedded Signup path.** There is no self-service Cloud API setup option for Rio customers — you will always connect your WABA through Rio's onboarding interface. Rio operates as a WhatsApp Business Solution Provider (BSP) and manages the API connection on your behalf.

---

heading: WABA vs. WhatsApp Business App
content:
## WABA vs. WhatsApp Business App

A common source of confusion: "WhatsApp Business Account" is used casually to describe both the mobile app and the API account. They are different things.

| | WhatsApp Business App | WhatsApp Business Account (WABA) |
|---|---|---|
| What it is | Free mobile app (App Store/Play Store) | API account inside Meta Business Manager |
| Requires Meta Business Manager? | No | Yes |
| Used for | Direct mobile messaging | API-powered messaging at scale |
| Sufficient for Rio? | No | Yes — required |

Using the WhatsApp Business App alone does **not** mean a WABA exists. To use Rio, the customer needs a WABA inside Meta Business Manager with a registered phone number.

---

heading: How Rio Customers Set Up Their WABA
content:
## How Rio Customers Set Up Their WABA

Rio customers always set up their WABA through Rio's Embedded Signup flow — Rio acts as your WhatsApp Business Solution Provider (BSP) and manages the API connection on your behalf. You own the WABA inside your own Meta Business Portfolio; Rio is connected to it as your service provider.

This means:
- You do not need to create a Meta developer app or configure webhooks yourself
- You do not need to apply for any Meta app permissions — Rio handles this
- Your WABA and phone number remain yours; you can switch providers if needed

---

heading: Embedded Signup Flow
content:
## Embedded Signup Flow

Embedded Signup is Meta's browser-based flow that handles authentication, WABA creation, and phone number registration in one sequence. It runs inside a Meta-hosted popup window launched from the Rio onboarding interface.

**Overview of the flow:**

1. Customer logs into Rio and clicks "Connect with WhatsApp"
2. Rio launches a Meta Embedded Signup popup (via OAuth)
3. Customer authenticates with their Facebook account
4. Customer selects or creates a Meta Business Portfolio
5. Customer creates a new WABA (or selects an existing one)
6. Customer adds a phone number and completes OTP verification
7. Rio receives production credentials and the connection is established

**Key technical notes (per Meta official docs):**
- The popup session expires after 1 hour (per 360dialog docs)
- Do not close or reload the tab during signup — this breaks the flow (per ManyChat docs)
- Browser popups must be allowed in browser settings

---

heading: Creating vs. Selecting an Existing WABA
content:
## Creating vs. Selecting an Existing WABA

During Embedded Signup, the customer sees two options:

**Option 1: Create a new WABA**
- Meta creates a fresh WABA attached to the selected Business Portfolio
- Customer enters WABA name, business category, and phone number details
- This is the standard path for new setups

**Option 2: Select an existing WABA**
- Customer can connect an existing WABA to Rio during the signup flow
- This is used for businesses that already have a WABA from a previous provider or direct API setup
- The phone number still needs to be verified or migrated

According to Wati documentation: always create a new WABA when connecting to a new BSP for the first time — this avoids conflicts with existing WABA configurations. However, selecting an existing WABA is valid if you are connecting a clean WABA you already own.

---

heading: WABA Name vs. Display Name — What's the Difference?
content:
## WABA Name vs. Display Name — What's the Difference?

Many customers confuse these two names. They are different things:

| | WABA Name | Display Name |
|---|---|---|
| What it is | The internal name of your WhatsApp Business Account in Meta Business Manager | The business name your customers see in WhatsApp chats |
| Who sees it | You and Rio (internal only; not visible to your customers) | Your customers — shown in the chat header instead of your phone number |
| Example | "Acme Corp WABA" | "Acme Corp" |
| Reviewed by Meta? | No | Yes — goes through Meta's display name approval process |

**Your display name is what matters to your customers.** It is the name that appears in their WhatsApp inbox, e.g., "Acme Corp" instead of "+62 812 3456 7890". Choose it carefully — display names are strictly reviewed by Meta and changes after registration require a 30-day waiting period. See 04-display-name.md for full rules.

---

heading: WABA Creation Branches (from Rio Embedded Signup Flow)
content:
## WABA Creation Branches (from Rio Embedded Signup Flow)

During the Rio Embedded Signup flow, after Facebook login, the customer faces a branch:

**Branch A: Connect a WhatsApp Business App**
- Used when the customer already has an active WhatsApp Business App account and wants to use Coexistence
- Requires WhatsApp Business App version 2.24.17 or later
- Phone number must have 7+ days of activity on the app
- Not available in all regions (see 03-phone-number-setup.md for coexistence details)

**Branch B: Create a WhatsApp Business Account (WABA)**
- Standard path for new API connections
- Customer creates a new WABA, enters display name, selects category, and adds a phone number
- Display names are noted as "very strict" in the Rio Notion walkthrough — see 04-display-name.md

After Branch B, the flow proceeds to:
1. Create a Business Portfolio (if none exists) or select an existing one
2. Create a new WABA under that portfolio
3. Enter display name and business category
4. Add and verify a phone number via OTP

---

heading: Partner Conflict: Existing WABA Locked to Another BSP
content:
## Partner Conflict: Existing WABA Locked to Another BSP

If a customer's phone number or WABA is already attached to another BSP (ManyChat, Wati, 360dialog, etc.), Rio cannot claim it until the previous partner releases it.

**From Rio Notion docs:** The number may be attached to ManyChat, Wati, or another partner — this creates a "partner lock" that prevents new connection.

**How to resolve (per Rio sign-up walkthrough):**
- Go to Meta Business Suite > Business Settings > Partners
- Disconnect the previous partner from the WABA or phone number
- URL for managing partners: https://business.facebook.com/select/?next=https%3A%2F%2Fbusiness.facebook.com%2Fsettings%2Fpartners

**Additional steps from competitor docs:**
- After disconnecting from a previous BSP, wait 24-48 hours before reconnecting (per ManyChat docs)
- For credit line conflicts (especially relevant when switching from ManyChat): remove the previous BSP's credit line from the WABA in Meta Business Manager > Billing > Credit Lines

---

heading: Phone Number Limits Per WABA
content:
## Phone Number Limits Per WABA

Per Meta official and 360dialog documentation:
- A single WABA starts with **2 registered phone numbers** (expandable to 20)
- Expanding beyond 2 requires completing Meta Business Verification (see 01-prerequisites.md)

Per Respond.io documentation:
- Unverified accounts: up to **2 phone numbers**
- Verified accounts: up to **20 phone numbers**

---

heading: WABA Currency Requirement
content:
## WABA Currency Requirement

Your WABA and Meta Business Manager must have their currency set to **USD**. A currency mismatch can cause messages to fail even after a successful connection to Rio.

**Billing note:** Rio uses Meta's per-message pricing (PMP) model. The older conversation-based pricing (CBP) model was deprecated as of July 1, 2025. Meta charges per message sent; pricing varies by message type and country. Rio will provide current rate information.

---

heading: Common Creation Errors
content:
## Common Creation Errors

### Common Issues

- **Issue**: Embedded Signup popup blocked by browser
  - **Symptom**: Clicking "Connect with WhatsApp" does nothing or popup is immediately closed
  - **Cause**: Browser is blocking popup windows
  - **Fix**: Allow popups from the Rio domain in browser settings; clear cache and cookies; try in a different browser

- **Issue**: "Embedded Signup was cancelled"
  - **Symptom**: Signup process stops; error message about cancellation appears
  - **Cause**: Popup window was closed accidentally; user denied permissions; Facebook login failed or expired; browser blocked popup
  - **Fix**: Allow popups in browser settings; log out of Facebook and back in; restart signup from the beginning; keep all windows open until the process completes

- **Issue**: Tab was closed or reloaded mid-flow
  - **Symptom**: Progress lost; OTP not received; setup incomplete
  - **Cause**: Closing or reloading the signup tab resets the session
  - **Fix**: Must restart the entire signup process from the beginning (per ManyChat docs)

- **Issue**: Partner lock — number tied to another BSP
  - **Symptom**: Error during phone number setup, similar to: "The phone number you have entered is not associated with the business you selected"
  - **Error code**: `#3441041:019cfb0a-ee46-71b3-b945-f968ee2e3dea` (seen in Rio walkthrough)
  - **Cause**: Phone number already shared with ManyChat, Twilio, 360dialog, or another partner
  - **Fix**: Go to Meta Business Suite > Business Settings > Partners > disconnect the previous partner; wait 24-48 hours; retry

- **Issue**: Business Portfolio is agency-owned
  - **Symptom**: Cannot create WABA; Embedded Signup flow rejects or blocks asset creation
  - **Cause**: Customer's Business Portfolio is under an agency's control, not the business itself
  - **Fix**: Create a new Business Portfolio owned by the business; redo signup with the new portfolio

- **Issue**: Account disabled during signup due to Commerce Policy
  - **Symptom**: "This account was disabled because the website indicated in your Business Manager profile does not contain the necessary information to determine that your business complies with our Commerce Policy"
  - **Cause**: Business website missing required information; incomplete Business Manager profile; business sells prohibited items
  - **Fix**: Update website with address, phone, email, social links, product/service description, and copyright notice; update Business Manager with matching info; verify business is in a permitted category; resubmit for review

- **Issue**: Cannot select existing WABA — wrong Business Portfolio
  - **Symptom**: Existing WABA not visible in Embedded Signup dropdown
  - **Cause**: The customer authenticated with a Facebook account that doesn't have admin access to the Business Portfolio containing the WABA
  - **Fix**: Log out and log in with the correct Facebook account that has admin access to the right portfolio

- **Issue**: Coexistence "Phone number isn't allowed to connect"
  - **Symptom**: When choosing the WhatsApp Business App branch, error: "Phone number isn't allowed to connect"
  - **Cause**: Account does not meet Meta's requirement of prior activity in WhatsApp Business Manager; new accounts cannot use Coexistence
  - **Fix**: Use the standard "Create a WhatsApp Business Account" branch instead; or establish WABA history and retry Coexistence later

heading: Phone Number Registration and Setup
content:
# Phone Number Registration and Setup

> Last updated: 2026-03-20 | Sources: Notion (Rio), 360dialog, Wati, ManyChat, Respond.io, Infobip, Meta Official

heading: Overview
content:
## Overview

Setting up your phone number with Rio is a multi-step process: you prove you control the number via OTP, Meta attaches it to your WABA, registers it for API use, and you set a 6-digit two-step verification PIN. This is different from simply "using WhatsApp" — a number on the WhatsApp Business App is not the same as a number registered for Cloud API. This file covers what types of numbers work, the OTP process, registration steps, the 2-step PIN, number porting, and what commonly blocks registration.

---

heading: Customer States: Where They Can Be
content:
## Customer States: Where They Can Be

Your phone number can be in one of four states before connecting to Rio (per Rio Notion docs):

| State | Description | Ready for Rio? |
|---|---|---|
| State A | Number on WhatsApp Business App only | No — not yet API-registered |
| State B | Has a WABA but number not yet OTP-verified or registered | Partway there — needs completion; see 02-waba-creation.md |
| State C | Number is OTP-verified and Cloud API registered | Yes |
| State D | Number is registered with another BSP or partner | No — needs migration or release first; see 02-waba-creation.md |

The target state is C: "A phone number that Meta recognizes as owned by the business and registered inside a WABA for Cloud API messaging."

---

heading: Number Types Supported
content:
## Number Types Supported

### What Works Reliably (Recommended)

**Mobile numbers (standard SIM cards):**
- Any standard mobile SIM worldwide
- Indonesia: Telkomsel, XL Axiata, Indosat Ooredoo
- US: AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile
- Requirement: must be able to receive SMS or voice OTP

**Landlines (also work):**
- Standard business landlines in any country
- Indonesia: Telkom Indonesia landlines
- Requirement: must be able to receive a voice call with the OTP — landlines cannot receive SMS, so voice OTP must be available

### What Is Risky or Inconsistent

**API VoIP providers (sometimes works, often causes problems):**
- Twilio numbers
- Vonage (Nexmo)
- Plivo
- MessageBird virtual numbers

These may work if the voice OTP succeeds and the number is classified as "landline-like," but they are not reliable for long-term production use and can break later (limits, flags, approvals) — per Rio Notion VOIP Numbers Info.

According to Wati documentation: these are "generally NOT recommended (unreliable OTP delivery). Use only if can directly receive SMS or voice calls without IVR."

### What Does NOT Work

**App-based and cheap virtual numbers:**
- Google Voice
- Skype Number
- TextNow
- Burner / Hushed
- Dingtone / 2ndLine
- Free or cheap virtual number apps

These consistently fail OTP verification, block registration, or cause later account issues. Per Rio Notion: "Use a real mobile or landline number. Virtual numbers like Google Voice will not work reliably."

**Additional rules from competitor docs:**

- Numbers behind IVR systems with no ability to route OTP calls (Wati, 360dialog)
- Short codes — not eligible (Infobip)
- Toll-free numbers that cannot directly receive SMS or voice calls (Wati)
- Numbers currently linked to existing WhatsApp accounts (personal or business app)
- Numbers in restricted countries: Crimea, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria (Respond.io)

**Simple rule (from Rio Notion):**
- App-based / virtual number → Not supported
- API VoIP → Risky, inconsistent
- Real SIM or landline → Recommended

---

heading: Key Number Eligibility Requirements
content:
## Key Number Eligibility Requirements

A phone number must meet all of these criteria (synthesized across sources):

1. **Valid format**: Include country code in E.164 format (e.g., +1 555 123 4567)
2. **Can receive communications**: Must be capable of receiving voice calls for OTP verification, OR SMS for OTP verification
3. **Not currently on WhatsApp**: Must not be associated with any WhatsApp application (personal or business app) — must be in UNVERIFIED status before the registration API step, or the previous account must be deleted first
4. **Not locked to another partner**: Must not be currently shared with ManyChat, Wati, 360dialog, or another BSP
5. **Not behind IVR without routing**: IVR-routed numbers cannot receive OTPs unless the IVR is temporarily disabled or sender IDs are whitelisted

**Regarding numbers previously on WhatsApp Business App:**
- According to Wati: a mobile number previously registered on WhatsApp must remain inactive for a minimum of 6 months before use with the API if it was disconnected without following the proper unlink procedure. **This 6-month figure is likely specific to improperly disconnected accounts.** Current guidance across most sources is 24–48 hours after proper deregistration. If you properly unlinked or deleted the WhatsApp account on the number, the wait is typically 24–48 hours, not 6 months. Contact Rio support if you are unsure which procedure was followed.
- If using the Coexistence path, the number must have 7+ days of activity on the WhatsApp Business App (version 2.24.17 or later)

---

heading: OTP Verification Process
content:
## OTP Verification Process

Phone ownership verification is the first of two checks on the number. Meta sends a one-time code by SMS or voice call to prove the business controls the number.

**Two separate checks occur (per Rio Notion docs):**

1. **Phone ownership verification**: OTP sent by SMS or voice call; business enters code to prove control
2. **Platform registration**: After OTP, the number is registered for Cloud API use (a separate step)

**OTP delivery methods:**
- **SMS**: 6-digit code sent via text message
- **Voice call**: Automated call reads the 6-digit code aloud (required for landlines; useful as fallback when SMS fails)

**OTP expiry:**
- Codes expire after approximately 10 minutes (Respond.io)
- 360dialog: 2-minute cooldown required between verification attempts; 3 failed attempts trigger 2-hour lockout
- Meta official: limited number of OTP verification attempts allowed per phone number; exceeded attempts trigger security lockout

---

heading: Registration Steps
content:
## Registration Steps

The complete flow when setting up your number with Rio (per Rio Notion docs):

1. Create or connect your WABA through Rio's Embedded Signup (see 02-waba-creation.md)
2. Add your business phone number in WhatsApp Manager
3. Request OTP by SMS or voice call
4. Enter OTP to verify ownership
5. Register the number for Cloud API
6. Set the 6-digit two-step verification PIN
7. Your number is now connected — you can send and receive through Rio

---

heading: Two-Step Verification PIN
content:
## Two-Step Verification PIN

**Required for all registrations.** After OTP verification, the business must set a 6-digit PIN that protects the phone number registration from unauthorized access.

**PIN details (per Meta official docs):**
- Format: 6-digit number chosen by the user
- Confirmed by re-entry
- Required during phone number registration on any new device or account
- Prevents account hijacking even if an SMS code is compromised
- Optional: provide a recovery email to enable PIN reset if forgotten

**Conflict scenario:** If the number already has a 2-step PIN from a previous setup and the person onboarding does not know it, Meta will require the PIN before allowing re-registration. This is a common failure point. Resolution: contact the previous BSP or Meta support, or wait for the account reset period.

**For BSP migration (per Meta official and Respond.io docs):** Two-step verification must be **disabled** on the source WABA before migrating a phone number to a new BSP. After migration completes, it can be re-enabled.

---

heading: Number Porting
content:
## Number Porting

Porting a number from one BSP to another preserves key attributes. Per Respond.io's migration documentation:

**What transfers during BSP migration:**
- Display name (if approved)
- Phone number quality rating
- Messaging tier level
- Official Business Account status (blue tick, if applicable)
- High-quality approved message templates
- Open conversation windows and 24-hour service window timer

**What does NOT transfer:**
- Low-quality, rejected, or pending templates
- Message history from On-Premises API sources
- Chat history from WhatsApp Business App

**Migration pre-requirements (per Respond.io and Meta official docs):**
- Meta Business Manager account with admin access
- Business must be verified by Meta
- Phone number display name must be approved
- Two-step verification must be disabled on the phone number before migration
- Sufficient phone number slots available in the destination WABA
- Access to receive OTP via SMS or phone call

**Migration timeline:** Respond.io states migration completes within 5 minutes with no downtime — messages sent during migration are received once migration completes.

---

heading: What Blocks Registration Most Often
content:
## What Blocks Registration Most Often

Per Rio Notion docs and confirmed across all competitor sources:

**1. Customer cannot receive the OTP**
- No SMS arrives, voice call fails, wrong number format, SIM not active, or call routing issues
- VOIP/virtual number fails OTP delivery
- IVR system blocks incoming calls from WhatsApp sender IDs

**2. Too many OTP attempts**
- Meta limits OTP verification attempts per phone number
- 3 failed attempts = 2-hour lockout (per 360dialog)
- 10 failed attempts = 72-hour lockout (per Respond.io)

**3. Two-step verification conflict**
- Number has an existing 2-step PIN from a previous setup that the onboarding person doesn't know
- Fix: must know the PIN, or wait for account reset, or contact Meta support

**4. Partner lock**
- Number is shared with ManyChat, Twilio, 360dialog, or another partner
- Rio cannot claim it until it is released or migrated

**5. Number still active on WhatsApp (personal or business app)**
- Meta blocks registration if the number is still logged in to WhatsApp on any device
- Must delete the WhatsApp account on that number before registering for API

**6. Wrong customer expectation**
- Customer believes "I already use WhatsApp Business App, so I'm done" — they are not done
- App usage alone does not register the number for API messaging (per Rio Notion docs)

**7. Waiting period after previous API disconnection**
- If a number was previously registered on API without proper disconnection, Wati recommends waiting 1-2 months before re-registration
- Meta official: wait at least 5 minutes after deleting a phone number from a WABA before re-registering (error code 133015: "Phone number cannot be registered")

---

heading: Coexistence (Using App and API Simultaneously)
content:
## Coexistence (Using App and API Simultaneously)

WhatsApp Coexistence allows a business to use the same phone number on both the WhatsApp Business App and the Cloud API at the same time. This is a specific supported flow — not universally available.

**Requirements for coexistence:**
- WhatsApp Business App version **2.24.17 or later** (Wati, Respond.io)
- Phone number must have **7+ days of activity** on the app before attempting coexistence (Wati)
- Business location must be in a supported region

**Regions where coexistence is NOT available (as of March 2026):**
- Per ManyChat: EU, UK, India, Japan, Nigeria, South Korea, Russia, South Africa, Philippines, Australia, Turkey
- Per Wati: Nigeria, South Africa (for coexistence)
- Per Respond.io: EU, UK, Australia, Japan, Philippines, Turkey, South Korea

**Regions where coexistence IS available:**
- Per ManyChat: US, Brazil, LATAM, Israel
- Per Wati: India, Brazil, Mexico, Indonesia, US, Hong Kong, Singapore

> **Note — India coexistence conflict:** ManyChat lists India as NOT supported for coexistence; Wati lists India as supported. These sources contradict each other as of March 2026. **Do not advise Indian customers on the coexistence path without first verifying with Rio support.** The same applies to Indonesian customers given the uncertainty across sources.

**Important maintenance rule (per Respond.io):** Must open the WhatsApp Business App at least once every 14 days to maintain active connection. Failure removes the channel connection.

**Features disabled after enabling coexistence (per Respond.io, ManyChat, Wati):**
- Broadcast lists creation
- Message edit/revoke in 1:1 chats
- Disappearing messages
- View-once messages
- Live location sharing
- Group chats (not synced to API)

---

heading: Common Issues
content:
## Common Issues

### Common Issues

- **Issue**: OTP not received via SMS
  - **Symptom**: No text message arrives after requesting OTP
  - **Cause**: Virtual/VOIP number, carrier blocking, IVR interference, DND enabled, international SMS not enabled
  - **Fix**: Switch to voice call verification; disable call forwarding and IVR; wait 2 minutes between attempts; contact carrier to whitelist Meta SMS sender; if using VOIP number, switch to a real SIM

- **Issue**: OTP not received via voice call
  - **Symptom**: No call arrives after requesting voice OTP
  - **Cause**: IVR system blocking incoming calls from WhatsApp sender IDs (typically +1 US or +44 UK)
  - **Fix** (per 360dialog): Whitelist +1 and +44 sender IDs in IVR; temporarily disable IVR during the 15-minute registration window; retry after whitelisting

- **Issue**: Account locked after too many OTP attempts
  - **Symptom**: System blocks further attempts with lockout message
  - **Cause**: 3 failed attempts (2-hour lockout per 360dialog) or 10 failed attempts (72-hour lockout per Respond.io)
  - **Fix**: Wait for the lockout period to expire; retry with alternate verification method after unlock

- **Issue**: Error code 133015 — "Phone number cannot be registered"
  - **Symptom**: Registration fails immediately
  - **Cause**: Phone number was recently deleted from the WABA and has not completed its cooldown period
  - **Fix**: Wait at least 5 minutes after deletion before re-registering; verify number is not active on any WhatsApp app; retry registration

- **Issue**: Error — "App Not Deleted" / Error 1005 (360dialog)
  - **Symptom**: Registration attempt fails with error code 1005
  - **Cause**: Personal WhatsApp or WhatsApp Business App is still installed and active on the device
  - **Fix**: Fully uninstall and delete WhatsApp/WhatsApp Business App; clear app cache; restart phone; retry registration

- **Issue**: Partner error — number associated with wrong business
  - **Error message**: "The phone number you have entered is not associated with the business you selected. To continue, you need to unlink this phone number from that business or enter a different number." (Error `#3441041:019cfb0a-ee46-71b3-b945-f968ee2e3dea`)
  - **Symptom**: Registration blocked during embedded signup
  - **Cause**: Number is attached to a different Business Portfolio or partner than the one being used in the current signup
  - **Fix**: Go to Meta Business Suite > Partners > disconnect previous partner; unlink the number from the previous business context; retry

- **Issue**: Two-step PIN conflict
  - **Symptom**: Registration blocked because an existing PIN is required
  - **Cause**: Number has a 2-step verification PIN set from a previous setup; onboarding person does not know the PIN
  - **Fix**: Retrieve PIN from whoever set it up previously; if PIN is unknown, contact Meta support; for migrations, the previous BSP must disable 2-step verification before migration

- **Issue**: Coexistence "phone number isn't eligible"
  - **Error message**: "Your phone number isn't eligible to connect to the WhatsApp Business Platform"
  - **Symptom**: Coexistence setup blocked
  - **Cause**: Number lacks 7+ days of activity on WhatsApp Business App
  - **Fix**: Use number actively on the WhatsApp Business App for 7-30+ days before attempting coexistence; do not re-register (resets activity history); delete previous WABA configurations; wait 1-2 months before retrying

heading: Your Display Name on Rio's WhatsApp Service
content:
# Your Display Name on Rio's WhatsApp Service

> Last updated: 2026-03-20 | Sources: Notion (Rio), 360dialog, Wati, ManyChat, Respond.io, Infobip, Meta Official

heading: Overview
content:
## Overview

Your display name is the business name your customers see in WhatsApp instead of your phone number. For example, your customers will see "Acme Corp" in their chat instead of "+62 812 3456 7890." It appears in the sender field and in the business profile.

Display names go through a Meta review process and can be rejected — this is one of the most common friction points during WABA setup. Rio's onboarding notes: "Display Names are very strict." Meta's policy is documented at https://www.facebook.com/business/help/338047025165344 and https://www.facebook.com/business/help/757569725593362.

---

heading: Meta's Display Name Policy
content:
## Meta's Display Name Policy

### Core Requirements

- **Minimum 3 characters** (Meta official)
- **Must represent the business, service, product, or department** — not a slogan, not an individual person's full name, not a generic industry term
- **Must comply with WhatsApp Commerce and Business policies**
- **Must have a working, live business website** — display name approval requires an active website (Meta official, 360dialog, ManyChat)
- **One display name per phone number** — each phone number under your WABA has its own display name; you cannot have multiple display names for a single number

### Branding Consistency Requirements

The display name must be consistent with the business's external branding. This is checked against:
- The business website
- Social media presence
- Company registration name

According to 360dialog documentation:
- Capitalization and spacing matter exactly: "BrandName", "Brandname", "brandname", "BRANDNAME", and "Brand Name" are all treated as different variations
- Must align with company website and marketing materials
- Must maintain grammatically correct capitalization

According to Wati documentation:
- Display name should appear on the business website, typically in the copyright footer
- Example format: `© [Display Name] Year. All rights reserved.`
- Use the same language for both the website and the display name (if website is in Arabic, display name must be in Arabic)

According to Respond.io documentation:
- Use clear, specific business identifiers — "Acme Co – California" is preferred over generic "Acme"
- Consistency across Meta Business Manager, WABA, and Ad Account improves verification chances

---

heading: Formatting Rules
content:
## Formatting Rules

Per Meta official documentation:

- Proper capitalization required
- Limited punctuation allowed
- No URLs permitted in the display name
- No emojis, @, #, asterisks, or symbols not part of official branding (per ManyChat and 360dialog)
- No special characters beyond what appears in the registered business name
- Simple text format: letters, numbers, spaces

---

heading: What Gets Rejected
content:
## What Gets Rejected

Display names are rejected when they fall into any of these categories:

### Prohibited content (Meta official and all BSPs):

| Rejection reason | Example | Why rejected |
|---|---|---|
| Does not relate to business | "Tech Solutions" for a bakery | No clear business connection |
| Generic industry terms | "Fashion", "Technology", "Retail", "Restaurant" | Too generic to identify a specific business |
| Geographic locations | "New York", "California", "Jakarta" | Not a business name |
| Claim terms | "Official", "Verified", "Authorized" | False authority signal |
| Meta product names | "WhatsApp", "Facebook", "Instagram", "Messenger" | Prohibited (implies Meta affiliation) |
| Individual's full name | "John Smith" | Not a business name |
| Long slogans | "Your Best Partner for Quality Solutions Since 1995" | Slogan format, not a name |
| No active website | Any name submitted without live website | Cannot approve without website |
| Commerce Policy violation | Name tied to prohibited products (gambling, adult content, alcohol, drugs) | Policy non-compliance |
| Special characters | "Joe's #1 Shop!" | Special characters outside official branding |
| Mismatched language | English name with Arabic-language website | Language inconsistency |

### Subsidiary/partnership situations (per 360dialog docs):

If the legal entity name differs from the display name, the relationship must be documented on the company website. For example: "Business ABC powered by business CDE" in the website footer. If the connection between the display name and the business is not obvious from the website, use the format "by [company name]" in the display name.

---

heading: How to Choose a Compliant Display Name
content:
## How to Choose a Compliant Display Name

**Good candidates:**
- The exact legal registered business name
- A well-known brand name that appears consistently on the website
- A department name within a large company (e.g., "Acme Corp Support" or "Acme Corp – Bali")

**Process before submitting:**
1. Check that the name appears on the business website (homepage, footer, or About page)
2. Verify the exact capitalization and spacing matches the website
3. Confirm the name does not contain any prohibited words or characters
4. Confirm the business website is live, accessible, and has SSL
5. Confirm the business complies with WhatsApp Commerce Policy (no prohibited product categories)

**Language consistency rule (Wati docs):** The language of the display name must match the language of the business website. A bilingual website may allow flexibility, but the primary display language should match.

---

heading: Approval Process and Timeline
content:
## Approval Process and Timeline

Display name review happens as part of WABA creation, during or after phone number registration.

**Typical approval flow:**
1. Display name submitted during Embedded Signup or WhatsApp Manager setup
2. Meta reviews against Commerce Policy and display name guidelines
3. Status becomes "Approved", "Pending", or "Rejected"

**Status meanings (per ManyChat docs):**
- **Approved**: Display name active; full functionality enabled
- **Pending**: Under review; messaging may continue with some limits
- **Rejected**: Does not meet guidelines; must change name immediately

**Timeline:**
- Fast track: a few minutes to a few hours for AI-reviewed names (Meta official)
- Standard: 24+ hours for names requiring manual review
- After rejection and resubmission: additional 24+ hours

Per 360dialog documentation:
- Prior to registration, display names can be changed unlimited times
- After registration: a **30-day waiting period** is required between name changes

Per Wati documentation:
- Meta reviews display names after the account reaches a **2,000 messaging limit** in some cases — this behavior is likely outdated and tied to an older messaging tier system; treat early rejection messages as real and address them promptly
- Display name may become locked after coexistence activation

**Impact of unapproved display name:**
- Unverified/unapproved: messaging limited to 250 conversations/month (ManyChat)
- Approved: messaging limit increases to 1,000+ conversations/month
- Cannot apply for Official Business Account (OBA / blue tick) without an approved display name (Wati)

---

heading: Appeal Process
content:
## Appeal Process

If a display name is rejected:

**Per Meta official documentation:**
- A limited number of appeals are allowed per review period
- After exhausting appeals: a **7-60 day cooldown** before retrying
- Appeals should include evidence of business legitimacy and brand consistency

**Per Wati documentation:**
- Cannot apply for OBA (blue tick) without display name approval
- OBA applications must go through the BSP

**Steps to appeal or resubmit:**
1. Review the rejection reason in Meta Business Suite or WhatsApp Manager
2. Modify the display name to address the specific rejection reason
3. Ensure the new name appears on the business website
4. Resubmit for approval
5. Wait 24+ hours for the new name to be reviewed
6. Do not repeatedly resubmit — submit one change at a time and wait (ManyChat)

---

heading: Change Process
content:
## Change Process

### Before phone number registration:
- Display name can be changed freely (unlimited changes per 360dialog)

### After phone number registration:
- **If your account has OBA (Official Business Account / blue tick) status:** Do not change your display name without contacting Rio support first. Changing the display name after OBA approval risks losing OBA status and requires Meta's explicit re-approval. This is not guaranteed and may take weeks.
- 360dialog: **30-day waiting period** between changes
- ManyChat: submit through Settings → WhatsApp → pencil icon; takes 24+ hours for approval; one change at a time
- Wati: changes after coexistence activation may require Meta approval and are not guaranteed
- Respond.io: changing display name requires reapproval and should be planned carefully before going live

### How to change in WhatsApp Manager directly:
- Go to Meta Business Suite > WhatsApp Manager > Phone Numbers
- Select the number
- Edit display name
- Submit for approval

---

heading: Common Issues
content:
## Common Issues

### Common Issues

- **Issue**: Display name rejected — policy violation
  - **Symptom**: Status shows "Rejected" in Meta Business Suite or WhatsApp Manager
  - **Cause**: Name contains prohibited content (Meta product names, generic terms, geographic locations, claim terms, slogans, individual person's name, special characters)
  - **Fix**: Review rejection reason; replace with official legal business name containing only letters, numbers, and spaces; resubmit

- **Issue**: Display name rejected — branding mismatch
  - **Symptom**: Name rejected even though it appears on the website
  - **Cause**: Capitalization or spacing differs from official branding; unauthorized abbreviations or symbols included
  - **Fix** (per 360dialog): Match exact capitalization, spacing, and formatting from official branding; remove abbreviations and symbols not used in official brand identity; resubmit

- **Issue**: Display name rejected — no working website
  - **Symptom**: Cannot approve display name; error about missing website
  - **Cause**: Website not live, not registered in Meta Business Portfolio, or not related to the business
  - **Fix**: Ensure website is live and SSL-secured; register website URL in Meta Business Portfolio; ensure website clearly shows business name, address, and contact info; retry

- **Issue**: Subsidiary or partnership relationship not recognized
  - **Symptom**: Display name rejected because Meta cannot find a connection between the name and the website
  - **Cause**: The display name refers to a subsidiary or partner entity whose relationship to the registered business is not documented online
  - **Fix** (per 360dialog): Update both company websites to document the relationship (e.g., add "Business ABC powered by Business CDE" to website footer); provide documentation links in appeal

- **Issue**: Cannot update display name — stuck in loop
  - **Symptom**: Display name rejected but change doesn't reflect in interface; appears stuck
  - **Cause**: Approval process is asynchronous; changes take time to reflect; multiple resubmissions may conflict
  - **Fix** (per ManyChat): Hover over display name field; click pencil icon; enter compliant name; submit once; wait 24+ hours; do not resubmit until current review completes

- **Issue**: Display name locked after coexistence activation
  - **Symptom**: Cannot change business name after enabling coexistence
  - **Cause**: Meta locks name for consistency across platforms after coexistence is activated
  - **Fix** (per Wati): Verify and finalize display name before enabling coexistence; contact Meta/BSP support for post-activation changes (approval not guaranteed); plan to deactivate and re-setup if name change is critical

- **Issue**: Language mismatch rejection
  - **Symptom**: Display name rejected; inconsistent language noted
  - **Cause**: Website is in one language but display name is in a different language
  - **Fix** (per Wati): Match the language of the display name to the primary language of the business website; update website or display name to be consistent

heading: Business Verification for Rio's WhatsApp Service
content:
# Business Verification for Rio's WhatsApp Service

> Last updated: 2026-03-20 | Sources: Notion (Rio), 360dialog, Wati, ManyChat, Respond.io, Infobip, Meta Official

heading: Overview
content:
## Overview

Meta Business Verification is the process of confirming that your business is legitimate by submitting legal documents to Meta's Security Center. It is not always required to start onboarding with Rio, but it gates higher messaging limits, the ability to register more than 2 phone numbers, and full platform capabilities. Verification is completed through Meta Business Suite directly by you — Rio will guide you through the process but does not submit documents on your behalf for standard business verification.

---

heading: What Is Business Verification
content:
## What Is Business Verification

Business verification is a Meta-side process where Meta reviews submitted legal documents against the business information registered in Meta Business Manager. A verified business receives a verification badge inside Meta Business Manager and gains access to higher-tier features on the WhatsApp Business Platform.

It is distinct from:
- **Phone number OTP verification** — proving you control a phone number
- **Display name approval** — Meta approving the sender name shown to customers
- **Official Business Account (OBA) / Blue Tick** — a separate, higher-level status requiring media coverage and brand recognition

---

heading: When Business Verification Is Required
content:
## When Business Verification Is Required

**Not required to begin onboarding.** A WABA can be created and a number registered without a verified business.

**Required or strongly recommended when:**
- The business wants to register more than 2 phone numbers (unverified accounts are limited to 2 numbers; verified accounts can have up to 20) — Source: Respond.io
- The business wants to send business-initiated (outbound) messages at scale — Source: ManyChat
- Meta triggers a verification requirement during Embedded Signup in certain cases — Source: Notion (Rio), meta-business-info.md
- The business applies for Official Business Account (OBA / Blue Tick) — Source: Wati
- The business wants to scale messaging beyond 250 conversations/month (ManyChat notes unverified accounts cap at 250 conversations/month vs 1,000+ after verification) — Source: ManyChat

**Messaging tier impact (Respond.io):**
- Limited Access Tier (new, unverified): 250 business-initiated conversations per 24-hour rolling period
- Verified Tier: 2,000 business-initiated conversations (automatic upon verification)
- Escalated tiers: 10,000 → 100,000 → Unlimited (require high quality rating + 50% utilization within 7 days)

---

heading: Where to Complete Verification
content:
## Where to Complete Verification

Meta Business Suite → Business Settings → Security Center → "Start Verification"

URL: https://www.facebook.com/business/help/2058515294227817

Official Meta doc: https://developers.facebook.com/docs/whatsapp/business-management-api/business-verification/

---

heading: What Meta Validates
content:
## What Meta Validates

Meta checks that the submitted documents match the information registered in Business Manager:
- Legal business name
- Business address
- Business phone number
- Business email address
- Website (must be live and match business details) — Source: Respond.io, Meta Official
